title: Pinnacle Health — Network fencing, egress controls & POC success criteria
summary: POC scoping focused on private connectivity (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), strict egress routing through customer-owned NAT/egress appliances, regional lockdown (US/EU), and measurable benchmarks for latency/throughput. Agreed baseline success criteria and a 6-week pilot plan; Redwood to deliver network runbook, security docs, and preliminary pricing. Next call: infra kick-off + test account provisioning.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-05 15:00 UTC | Duration 52m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya and Liam (Redwood SEs), Carlos (CTO), Maya (Head Eng), Anita (Security), Samir (Infra), Nadia (SRE)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick agenda — we want to confirm network topology options, residency/region requirements, and nail down success criteria for the pilot. Priya will walk through proposed benchmarks.
[00:22] Carlos: Cool, we mainly want zero internet egress from our private subnets. All model requests must egress via our perimeter firewall/appliance so we can inspect and log.
[00:34] Anita: And audit logs retained for 7 years, plus integration with our SIEM. Also SSO and RBAC stuff later.
[00:45] Priya: Understood. Two main connectivity patterns we're proposing: VPC peering (straight routing) or PrivateLink/Interface endpoints (managed ENIs). Peering is simple but cross-account routing can be messy for egress controls; PrivateLink gives you stronger isolation and you can pin egress through your NAT gateway.
[01:05] Maya: When you say pin egress through our NAT, you mean the model container will talk to our NAT and not touch the public internet at all?
[01:12] Priya: Right — traffic from the Redwood inference instances will route over the peering/PrivateLink into your VPC and then out only via the egress IPs you control. We also support SNAT-ing to your egress appliance.
[01:28] Samir: How does DNS resolve for model artifact pulls and container image pulls? We need to ensure no accidental egress during startup.
[01:35] Liam: Good point. For images we recommend pre-pulling images into your private registry in the pilot — that avoids out-of-band pulls. For model weights, Redwood can host them in a customer-controlled bucket (we can do an IAM role) or we can stage them in the private plane. There's a small setup step.
[01:55] Carlos: We're strongly leaning to PrivateLink because our security team wants fine-grained flow logs and we can attach NACLs and security appliances on that side. Any drawbacks?
[02:04] Priya: PrivateLink does add some operational overhead and you pay for interface endpoints, but it avoids transitive routing issues and keeps control in your VPC. Peering is cheaper but you must manage route tables carefully.
[02:20] Anita: Are there differences in egress IP stability? We need predictable source IPs for our vendor firewalls.
[02:26] Priya: With PrivateLink + your NAT the egress IPs are whatever your NAT provides — stable. With peering, same idea but if you autoscale NATs you might get multiple egress IPs; you can control that via an egress gateway.
[02:40] Nadia: What about region-locking? We need EU for EU patient data and US for US. Can Redwood pin inference to specific regions?
[02:49] Jordan: Yes, we can pin model serving to regions. For pilot we propose two separate pilot clusters — one in eu-west-1 and one in us-east-1. Data can be kept local; logs can be forwarded to your SIEM via private peering.
[03:05] Maya: Costs — will we be charged for cross-region traffic?
[03:09] Jordan: Cross-region egress will be billed and you'll see inter-region transfer costs; we'll call that out in pilot pricing. We can avoid cross-region traffic by keeping inference and storage in the same region.
[03:20] Priya: Moving to benchmarks — we propose three scenarios: 1) low-latency chat (256 token requests), 2) long-context summarization (8k tokens), 3) embeddings bulk (batched 512-request jobs). We'll measure p50/p95 latency, tokens/s, and token-cost.
[03:41] Carlos: Baseline numbers we need: p95 under 1s for chat is ideal, but we can accept up to 1.5s during pilot. Throughput target: 200 reqs/s for chat workload.
[03:53] Priya: We can target p50 ~120-180ms for small chat on an H100-backed instance, p95 depends on batching and cold-starts. For long-context tests we expect higher memory and will use larger GPUs or multiple-GPU config.
[04:09] Liam: Note transcription: measurements vary by model size and quantization. We'll run both fp16 and int8-ish quantized variants to show tradeoffs.
[04:24] Maya: For embeddings we want a nightly batch that processes 4M rows, roughly 4M calls. How long to run that in the pilot?
[04:33] Priya: For that scale we'll run a producer/consumer benchmark — estimate ~8 hours on 4xA100/80GB equivalent. We'll provide a runbook to scale and parallelize.
[04:46] Samir: IAM and keystore: we prefer BYOK (bring your own key). Any blockers?
[04:51] Jordan: Redwood supports KMS integrations and customer-managed keys for Private deployments; in hosted/pilot we'll offer envelope encryption and can integrate with your KMS via cross-account IAM roles for model artifacts and logs.
[05:08] Anita: Audit logs — we'd like an immutable stream to our SIEM and an S3 archive. Retention policy 7 years; CIA compliance. Do you have a hardened audit pipeline?
[05:18] Priya: We will stream audit events over private connection to your ingest endpoint and can write to an S3 bucket in your account or a dedicated S3 in region with cross-account replication. We'll include a sample lambda consumer.
[05:33] Carlos: Okay, what's the POC definition of success?
[05:36] Jordan: Proposal — success if all of the following are met: 1) network topology enforces zero public egress from private subnets for inference traffic, 2) baseline benchmarks meet agreed latency/throughput targets (p95 chat <=1.5s, throughput 200 req/s), 3) logs and audit stream into Pinnacle SIEM with retention and searchable fields, 4) security sign-off for encryption and KMS flow, 5) integration test: end-to-end inference flows from Pinnacle app through the fenced network and back.
[06:05] Maya: That looks good. Any quantitative SLOs on token accuracy/regression?
[06:11] Priya: We'll run a small eval prompt set and compare outputs against a baseline to detect quality regressions. We'll include a quality-monitoring step in the runbook.
[06:23] Samir: Network checklist? We need exact CIDRs, peering acceptance steps, PrivateLink endpoint subnets, route table docs, and expected ports.
[06:32] Priya: We'll send a runbook with step-by-step commands, Terraform snippets for PrivateLink and peering, and a minimal VPC template for the pilot.
[06:42] Liam: Also a note on egress TLS termination — if you want deep packet inspection we can route to your appliance which terminates TLS; otherwise use metadata tagging for logs.
[06:55] Anita: One more — SSO and SAML for the console and role-based access for token creation. We can't have engineers creating high-priv tokens without audit trails.
[07:05] Jordan: We support SAML and SCIM for provisioning; we'll map roles and create token-scoped permissions.
[07:13] Carlos: Timeline? How soon can we start?
[07:16] Jordan: Suggested 6-week pilot: Week 0 - kick-off and account provisioning; Week 1 - network config and peering/PrivateLink setup; Week 2 - small smoke tests and preload artifacts; Week 3 - baseline benchmarks; Week 4 - scale tests (embeddings bulk); Week 5 - security review & tuning; Week 6 - final sign-off and handoff. We can compress if Pinnacle wants.
[07:35] Maya: Resources from our side — Samir and Nadia will drive infra; Anita will do security sign-offs. CTO will be a sponsor.
[07:43] Jordan: Pricing — we'll send pilot pricing sheet. For PrivateLink there's an infra set-up fee plus per-hour instance time.
[07:50] Priya: For benchmarks we'll need a small test harness. We'll supply a repo with scripts and sample prompts. We ask you to expose an internal test endpoint for our scoring harness to post results to.
[08:05] Samir: Regarding certs and mutual TLS — can Redwood do mTLS on PrivateLink?
[08:10] Priya: Yes, we can support mTLS on the interface endpoints and require client certs. We'll document it.
[08:18] Nadia: One question — when traffic is routed into our VPC via PrivateLink are the source IPs preserved? We need to map requests back to caller for auditing.
[08:27] Liam: On PrivateLink the source will typically be the interface endpoint — but we can add X-Forwarded-For or preserve original identity in headers over private link. We'll include a signed header you can verify.
[08:40] Maya: Are there any limitations with multitenancy? We want strict tenant separation for patient PII.
[08:46] Priya: We run customer-dedicated namespaces for pilot; inference pods are single-tenant per customer. For multi-tenant customers we can discuss deeper isolation. For now you'll be single-tenant.
[08:58] Carlos: Anything else we need to consider for compliance?
[09:01] Anita: SOC2 Type II evidence, encryption at rest and in transit, KMS key lifecycle and rotation policy, and data sovereignty docs.
[09:10] Jordan: We'll attach security whitepaper and SOC2 cert. We'll also add the KMS integration guide.
[09:17] Priya: Quick operational note: we'll run a three-day baseline benchmark with synthetic and replay traffic to mirror production. We'll share dashboards in Redwood Console so you can watch token-level cost and latency.
[09:34] Maya: Good. For the embeddings job, we need a guaranteed SLA for completion time during the pilot. Can you commit to that?
[09:41] Jordan: We'll commit to a target completion window for the pilot and measure it. For production, SLA can be discussed on dedicated contracts.
[09:50] Carlos: Okay let's recap.
[09:52] Jordan: Recap: 1) Redwood to share runbook, PrivateLink/peering diagrams, and benchmark plan; 2) Pinnacle to send CIDRs and confirm regions (US/EU); 3) schedule infra kick-off for 8/12; 4) Redwood shares pricing and pilot contract; 5) Priya will own the benchmark scripts.
[10:12] Anita: We'll review the security docs and get back with any redlines.
[10:18] Jordan: Great — any final questions?
[10:21] Maya: Not from me.
[10:22] Carlos: Nothing else. Thanks everyone.
[10:25] Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up with the artifacts and set the infra kickoff.
[10:30] [End recording]

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-hearings around acronyms (NAT vs. NGT), person name spellings, and some audio overlap near the end.
